how_the_recorded_md5_was_reproduced.problem: the prereg records md5 d1a7b1cefc0031afa84e7b9334a08bc5 for zwfy6:.../A03_1B_base/per_example_mmlu.jsonl, but Pilot Zero and the guard classifier both read the EIGHT per-shard files, not the merged file. The two are not the same byte stream: a naive shard-order concatenation gives md5 759e8d639d388e652323d29f15cff197.
how_the_recorded_md5_was_reproduced.resolution: the canonical merged file is the shards merged and re-sorted by item_id. Reconstructing that byte stream from the eight shards reproduces md5 d1a7b1cefc0031afa84e7b9334a08bc5 EXACTLY, and sha256 8cbbb008f2f606b039d61f6fedfb54ae4b44aedf7430f9322fab3150027e2378, which equals the sha256sum of the merged file computed remotely on zwfy6 (.82, read-only ssh).
how_the_recorded_md5_was_reproduced.why_this_matters: it establishes that the analysis inputs (shards) and the pinned artefact (merged file) are the same data, so the md5 in the prereg does pin what the prereg says it pins. Without this the md5 documented one file while the numbers came from eight others.

d5_48_flip_reverification.question: does A04_MARGIN_GUARD_PREREG.md:212's '48 / 14,042 item flips' reproduce?
d5_48_flip_reverification.verdict: YES -- reproduces exactly, and so does every derived number.
d5_48_flip_reverification.method: both dumps merged from their own 8 shards, sorted by item_id, item_id and gold_letter sequences asserted identical, per-item content_norm correctness compared elementwise. No reimplementation of the metric: correctness taken from the harness-stored 'correct' flag.

prereg_values_for_comparison.match: all match to the precision printed in the prereg

NEW_numbers_the_prereg_did_not_report.note: the prereg reported flips on content_norm only. The same two dumps differ on the other two interfaces too, and by DIFFERENT amounts, which sharpens the 'a harness code change sits between the two evals' reading and rules out a single flipped subset.
NEW_numbers_the_prereg_did_not_report.reading: 80 items change PREDICTED option under content_norm while only 48 change correctness -- i.e. 32 prediction changes are wrong-to-wrong. The three interfaces disagree by 33/48/191 items, so the difference is not one bad shard or one truncated file; it is a scoring-path difference that touches all three interfaces with different sensitivity. This is consistent with the prereg's 'harness commit 7ac9653 falls strictly between the two evals' and remains, as the prereg says, NOT a proven causal attribution.

d5_48_flip_reverification.still_UNVERIFIED: causality. No same-code control was run (that would need GPU). The prereg's refusal to call this a 'noise floor' stands, and this pass does not weaken it. See memory note same-harness-runs-bit-identical: same-arch/same-harness re-runs in this repo are byte-identical, so a nonzero flip count REQUIRES a named cause and 'jitter' is not available as an explanation.
